Source: DriX-8 MCAP logs 04-09 Aug 2026 (EM2040 fitted) — 4.85 h steady cruise, flow meter vs thruster RPM.
Fuel law (through origin) L/H = 1.0038e-03·RPM -2.7743e-07·RPM² +2.4471e-10·RPM³  (R² 0.9996),
anchored by (0,0) and the measured 0.95 L/H station-keeping figure at ~1005 rpm.
Speed law (through origin) KNOTS = 0.003708·RPM  (R² 0.949; SOG-based, ±5-8% tidal).
Both agree with the primary in-band laws (planner model.json) to ≤3.7% in-window, 0.3% at 8 kt.
Drivetrain: direct drive, shaft rpm = engine rpm (trawling motor unused). 0 rpm = engine OFF = 0 L/H.
The engine idles at ~1000 rpm (≈0.95 L/H — the 1000 row) and engages at ~1100 minimum:
the 0-1000 rpm band is not an operating region; the curve merely passes through it.
† outside the cruise-measured 1400-3100 rpm window (extrapolated toward the idle/origin anchors).
PCT/HR is computed on the 250 L nominal tank (cell B16), which implies 2.50 L per indicated point.
THE GAUGE IS MEASURED AT 2.06 ± 0.11 L/POINT (72-86% band) — 4σ below that — so the needle
falls about 21% FASTER than this column shows. Set B16 = 206 to read PCT/HR on the measured scale.
The 25% floor is a needle position: on the measured scale a mission may spend about 154 L before reaching it, against 188 L on a linear tank.
Gauge non-linearity is UNRESOLVED (per-day spread only 1.5σ), not established; every reading is from the top third
of the tank and the reserve band itself has never been calibrated. See DriX8_Fuel_Gauge_Linearity.docx.
Full derivation: DriX_Fuel_Efficiency_Report §5.5 and the AndyMcLeod/DriX-Fuel-Planner repo.
